result:
All three artifacts are in place under `outputs/runs/run-03-dynamic-workflow/`:

- `proposal-acme-corp-2026-07-06.md` / `.docx` — customer-facing proposal
- `risk-assessment-acme-corp-2026-07-06.html` — interactive risk dashboard

**How the workflow was dynamic:** rather than mechanically spawning a fixed team, I triaged the RFP first and only then decided which specialists were warranted — in this case all four independent ones (technical fit, legal, pricing, competitive) were clearly triggered by explicit RFP content (scale/architecture asks, aggressive contract clauses, an explicit discount floor + MFN clause, and four named competitors). Those four ran in parallel; risk assessment ran as a dependent phase afterward since it needs the drafted proposal, not just the RFP. I also ran a conflict-check phase between specialist outputs (Legal wanted 60–90 days' termination notice vs. Pricing accepting the RFP's 30 days) and resolved it in Legal's favor per the deal-desk's standing policy of deferring to the more conservative/authoritative domain expert, without a costly follow-up round-trip.

**Bottom line:** technical fit is high; the deal is commercially attractive (~$650K–950K/year, 100/100 revenue score) but the risk dashboard flags net risk at 8.0% with 5 legal blockers as written (uncapped liability, unannounced audits, SLA/termination trigger, full IP vesting, subprocessor veto) — recommendation is **escalate to VP** to resolve those before submission rather than a clean proceed.
